cost_model.form: seconds(b) = a_node + c * (min(R, b) + A + m * [R > b]); no-think contact = the node's measured no-think mean seconds
cost_model.inputs: scripts/flights/nx/nxt_r2_cost_inputs.json (40 per-contact records of the NX-T R1 smoke: token counts, seconds, forced flag; no text)
cost_model.limits: four smoke rows, 12 thinking contacts per node; np4 batching jitter is inside the residual; defined for budgets up to the R1 budget 3,072

cost_estimate.fallback_note: The answer-only fallback adds at most one contact per budgeted-thinking contact: 5 per row (the delivering arm's 2 plus one per candidate node that still thinks); planned_model_calls is rows x (6 + 5) = 11880 (program maximum 6480). The runner requires only rows x (6 + 2). The FIT cap stays structural (rows x program contacts x endpoints = 25920).
cost_estimate.formula: expected = rows x arm mix / 1.84 rows per minute / 60 with the arm mix 2.46 delivering-row equivalents per row (perception-off-solver-3072 0.53 + solver-2048 0.93 + budget-3072 1.0); ceiling = ceil_0.1(expected x 1.3); each candidate cost is the clipped-reasoning model's predicted seconds per row relative to the delivering arm, rounded UP to 0.01
cost_estimate.reference_268b: one 268-B arm pass: 1,080 rows, 2,160 contacts, 9.78 GPU-h at 1.84 rows/min (spent about 9.4 against the 8.4 ceiling: the lesson of the measured-throughput rule)

findings.finding: NX-T R1 (which nodes need thinking at all) is still flying when this package is built, so the arm table is a DEFAULT: both nodes at 1,536 and both nodes at 2,048. R1's answer reshapes it: a node that reads NOT-NEEDED-AT-THE-FLOOR needs no budget scan, a node that reads NEEDS-THINKING is where the budget scan matters, and a one-node scan (e.g. Perception at 1,536 with the Solver at 3,072, or a node OFF) halves the round's question.
findings.remedy: the coordinator edits scripts/flights/nx/nxt_r2_arms.json after reading R1, re-runs nxt_r2_derive_cells.py and nxt_r2_write_registration.py; the derive proves only the thinking_variants block, the program id and the live-fit ids moved; everything else (ceiling, ids, texts, tests) follows the data.

findings.finding: Owner decision 313 A: no twin arm. The in-flight A/A offset on this core was measured twice (268-B SLU +1.15 / intent -0.09; P3.1 SLU -0.61 / intent +1.6), so the read judges every arm against the DECLARED offset |o| = 1.15 pp SLU (the larger of the two measured offsets) and the paired floor 0.7 pp; both are fixed here, before contact. A single-flight paired contrast cannot separate a real budget effect from np4 batching jitter below |o|: such an arm reads UNRESOLVED or CHEAPER-AT-NO-RESOLVED-LOSS, never a gain.
findings.remedy: none; the stage3_effect_floor_check design is same-flight-node-column with twin false (it accepts it).

findings.finding: Independent chains, no note sharing (coordinator ruling 2): the evidence, the instruction template and the QueryState are identical in every arm, but a non-delivering arm's Solver prompt carries THAT arm's Perception note, which a shorter Perception reasoning may write differently. A both-nodes arm therefore measures the budget of both nodes together with the downstream effect of the Perception note on the Solver; a one-node scan separates the two.
findings.remedy: none; stated so the attribution is not over-read.

findings.finding: The per-arm costs and the GPU-hour ceiling come from nxt_r2_cost.py, fitted on the 40 per-contact records of the NX-T R1 four-row smoke (12 thinking contacts per node). The model is the clipped-reasoning one (cost of a contact = intercept + slope x (min(natural reasoning, budget) + answer + forced-close message)); costs are rounded UP to 0.01 and the ceiling carries the registered 1.3 margin. The linear-in-budget guess is reported beside it as a LOWER reference (it under-states the cost of a lower budget).
findings.remedy: the R2 smoke measures the real mix; the reader's smoke stage compares it with the registered one and the coordinator signs off only when it is within 1.3x (decision 314 A condition).

findings.finding: Ruling 303 A: one experiment in flight. NX-T R1 occupies the Thinking session; this package is DRAFT / HELD until it has sealed and been read. The session is the 268-B think-budget-np4 session (budget 3072, cap 4096, same model fragment): no per-arm session, the per-request fields carry the arm.
findings.remedy: the coordinator flips the cells only after the R1 column flight has sealed.

findings.finding: As in the 268-B cells the model-free preflight counts the payload at 4 bytes per token (a placeholder) and would refuse the Solver render at the 4,096 cap; the cells defer to the registered exact per-contact context-fit gate (preflight_budget_mode defer-to-native-contact-fit), which runs on every arm's REAL request. A lower budget never lengthens a prompt: the cap stays 4,096 for every arm.

reasoning_budget_tokens and answer_reserve_tokens were already legal keys of a thinking_policy (receipt schema v5 unchanged). The one harness addition is the OPTIONAL thinking_frame.delivering_arm_id of the consumption module (rails/consumption_module.py), so the delivering arm is named budget-3072 instead of the carrier hook's both-on. Absent, the compiled block is byte-identical to NX-T R1's (unit-tested). consumption_module.py is not among the modules the prepared-artifact identity hashes (runtime, kb_policy, knowledge_provider, phase_supply, knowledge_stores), so merging it re-pins nothing by itself.

findings.finding: scripts/checks/flight_registration_check.py's node-column findings (aa-arm-missing, variant-cost-mismatch, template-summary-mismatch) read only the Solver's template_variants block and are a no-op for a Perception-node group; the declaration is nevertheless complete (variant_cost, template_variants summary with twin false) and stage3_effect_floor_check validates its shape.

prohibitions: No test-split, DEV or Fold A contact (TRAIN Fold B only).
No supply arm, no template column, no tool schema on any role; no Reviewer or Planner visit; max_revisions 0.

The system is the 268-B Thinking lock: the knowledge supply, the module graph, the post-processing and the roster are not changed. The per-node reasoning budget of the non-delivering arms is the ONLY varied factor.
The completion cap (4,096), the delivering arm's budget (3,072) and drop-reasoning-v1 never move; a candidate budget states its answer reserve (cap - budget).
No arm may set any knob other than enable_thinking / reasoning_budget_tokens / answer_reserve_tokens (rails.supply_variants.parse_perception_thinking_variants refuses the rest by name).
No twin arm and at most two candidate arms (owner decision 313 A).
No reasoning text is ever delivered, scored or carried to another node (reasoning_context_policy drop-reasoning-v1); a delivered reasoning marker stops the flight.
No benefit claim and no admission: claims_benefit is false; the read attributes a reasoning-budget cost to a node and reports the saving.
No flight before the coordinator countersigns the DRAFT rows, mints the decision receipt, the harness commit is on master, NX-T R1 has sealed and been read, and the cells are flipped.
No session is started by this registration. No paper-scale profile. No system-level claim.

words.CHEAPER-AT-NO-RESOLVED-LOSS: SLU CI95 lower bound >= -1.49 pp and intent CI95 lower bound >= -0.65 pp (decision 190 floors): any loss is inside the design's own resolution, so the cheaper budget may replace the locked one
words.GAIN: SLU CI95 lower bound above +|o| (the cheaper budget RAISES the score beyond the declared A/A width)
words.NEEDS-FULL-BUDGET: SLU CI95 upper bound below -|o| (the cheaper budget loses more than the declared A/A width)
words.UNRESOLVED: none of the above (the interval is too wide to call the budget cheaper at no loss, and the loss is not beyond |o|)
